evidenceDomains.title: Binary and Executable Artifacts
evidenceDomains.description: Visible binary and executable filesystem objects inspected as bounded artifacts.

evidenceDomains.title: Filesystem and Mount State
evidenceDomains.description: Filesystem paths, permissions, mounts, filesystems, and namespace-visible state.

evidenceDomains.title: Kernel and Privilege Interfaces
evidenceDomains.description: Kernel protocols, privilege interfaces, policy queries, and kernel-mediated side channels.

evidenceDomains.title: Process and Memory State
evidenceDomains.description: Procfs, process context, file descriptors, linker visibility, mappings, and memory state.

evidenceDomains.title: Runtime Injection and Code Integrity
evidenceDomains.description: Runtime instrumentation, injected components, hooks, and executable code integrity.

evidenceDomains.title: System Configuration and Security State
evidenceDomains.description: Properties, build identity, SELinux state, and other system security posture.

evidenceDomains.title: Package and Application Visibility
evidenceDomains.description: Package identities, application data paths, and package-associated storage visibility.

evidenceDomains.title: Hardware-backed Attestation and Trusted Execution
evidenceDomains.description: Android Keystore, attestation chains, RootOfTrust, and trusted execution state.

detections.name: Security Patch and Build Timestamp Coherence
detections.description: Compares each partition's declared Android security-patch level against the compile timestamp of that same partition, because a stock image declares a patch at most a few weeks after it was built. The comparison stays inside the property set and therefore survives a forged key attestation.

evidenceUnits.title: Declared patch level versus own build timestamp
evidenceUnits.observedObject: Per-partition pairs of security-patch level and build timestamp properties, such as ro.build.version.security_patch with ro.build.date.utc
evidenceUnits.proposition: A partition declares a security-patch level dated substantially later than the compile timestamp of that same partition, which no genuine build can produce
evidenceUnits.observationChannel: Bionic system property reads through __system_property_get
evidenceUnits.availability: Available when at least one partition publishes both a YYYY-MM-DD patch level and an epoch build timestamp; partitions publishing only one half are reported as not comparable
evidenceUnits.trustBoundary: Both values are read from the same property set, so this compares two values an attacker could control; it holds only because spoofing tools rewrite the patch level while leaving build timestamps intact
evidenceUnits.inferenceLimit: Proves the patch level was set after the image was produced but does not name the tool that set it; stock images legitimately declare a patch up to about two months after their build, so only skew far beyond that is graded, and an attacker who also rewrites build timestamps defeats the check entirely

detections.name: BusyBox Checking
detections.description: Classifies visible BusyBox paths by object type, resolved metadata, and bounded ELF-magic evidence without treating presence as proof of privilege.

evidenceUnits.title: Visible BusyBox artifact
evidenceUnits.observedObject: A resolved filesystem object at a BusyBox candidate path
evidenceUnits.proposition: A BusyBox-compatible artifact is visible through the app process filesystem view
evidenceUnits.observationChannel: Fixed-path access, lstat, O_PATH open, fstat, and bounded header inspection
evidenceUnits.availability: Available only for candidate paths visible and inspectable from the application sandbox
evidenceUnits.trustBoundary: App-local VFS view and user-space parsing can be filtered or hooked
evidenceUnits.inferenceLimit: Presence does not establish that the artifact grants privilege or was installed by a root framework

detections.name: Custom ROM Detection
detections.description: Checks build properties (test-keys, ro.debuggable, ro.secure) and known custom ROM identifiers (LineageOS, PixelExperience, etc.).

evidenceUnits.title: Custom or debug build fingerprint
evidenceUnits.observedObject: Build tags, debugging and security properties, and maintained ROM identifiers
evidenceUnits.proposition: An app-visible build value matches a maintained custom-ROM or debug-build rule
evidenceUnits.observationChannel: Android build and system-property observations
evidenceUnits.availability: Depends on property availability and the maintained identifier set
evidenceUnits.trustBoundary: Build and property values are user-space observations that can be spoofed
evidenceUnits.inferenceLimit: A custom or debug build is not equivalent to root or malicious tampering

detections.name: Dangerous Package Indicators
detections.description: Probes dangerous packages through PackageManager and visible native path indicators.

evidenceUnits.title: Package identity visibility
evidenceUnits.observedObject: An installed package identity queried through Android PackageManager
evidenceUnits.proposition: A package on the maintained dangerous-package indicator list is visible to the app
evidenceUnits.observationChannel: PackageManager queries subject to package visibility rules
evidenceUnits.availability: Depends on generated queries, installed package state, and platform visibility filtering
evidenceUnits.trustBoundary: PackageManager is a framework-mediated app-local view
evidenceUnits.inferenceLimit: A visible package can be inactive, renamed, cloned, or unrelated to current privilege state

evidenceUnits.title: Application data path visibility
evidenceUnits.observedObject: A canonical application data path derived from a maintained package identity
evidenceUnits.proposition: A package-derived private-data path is visible through the application filesystem view
evidenceUnits.observationChannel: Native access probes over canonical package-data paths
evidenceUnits.availability: Depends on package-data layout, namespace, permissions, and concealment affecting the app-local VFS view; under the app data isolation current Android enables, other applications' data directories are not visible and the unit reports itself unavailable
evidenceUnits.trustBoundary: Path resolution is mediated by the process mount namespace and kernel VFS
evidenceUnits.inferenceLimit: The path alone does not prove package activation, ownership, or granted privilege

detections.name: Security-Relevant System Properties
detections.description: Reports explicit insecure property values and a non-standard adb_enabled setting, with non-assessment emulator and ADB posture telemetry.

evidenceUnits.title: Security-relevant property posture
evidenceUnits.observedObject: Selected Android security and debugging property values
evidenceUnits.proposition: An available property value matches an explicitly defined insecure rule
evidenceUnits.observationChannel: Bionic system-property API
evidenceUnits.availability: Depends on property presence and successful property-service access
evidenceUnits.trustBoundary: User-space property APIs may be spoofed or hooked
evidenceUnits.inferenceLimit: An insecure value is contextual evidence and does not identify a root provider

evidenceUnits.title: Environment property posture
evidenceUnits.observedObject: Emulator and USB or ADB-related property values, and the Settings.Global adb_enabled value
evidenceUnits.proposition: adb_enabled holds a value outside {0, 1}, which neither the Settings UI nor AdbService writes; emulator and ADB-on posture is only described
evidenceUnits.observationChannel: Bionic system-property API and Settings.Global through the app ContentResolver
evidenceUnits.availability: Depends on property presence, successful property-service access, and a readable Settings.Global provider; from API 37 (Android 17 QPR1) the platform returns adb_enabled = 0 to third-party apps, so a 0 read there is recorded as redacted_by_platform and the rule is not evaluated
evidenceUnits.trustBoundary: User-space property APIs and in-process Settings reads may be spoofed or hooked, and the platform itself redacts adb_enabled for third-party apps from Android 17 QPR1
evidenceUnits.inferenceLimit: A non-standard adb_enabled value shows deliberate setting manipulation, not a root provider; a redacted_by_platform read is an unanswered channel, not ADB off, so the rule can fire only below API 37 or where the platform does not redact; emulator and ADB-on posture remain telemetry

detections.name: DRM Credential and Boot State Coherence
detections.description: Compares the boot state the device claims through its own properties against its Widevine credential. L1 key material is erased when a bootloader is unlocked and cannot be re-provisioned from userspace, so a device claiming a locked, verified boot state while advertising L1 with no provisioned credential is stating two things that cannot both be true.

evidenceUnits.title: Claimed boot state versus Widevine credential
evidenceUnits.observedObject: Widevine plugin securityLevel and systemId read through MediaDrm, and a session open attempt, compared against ro.boot.verifiedbootstate, ro.boot.flash.locked and ro.boot.vbmeta.device_state
evidenceUnits.proposition: A device claiming a locked and verified boot state advertises Widevine L1 while its plugin reports the unprovisioned-system-ID placeholder, which a genuinely locked device would not do
evidenceUnits.observationChannel: android.media.MediaDrm for the Widevine UUID via a JNI collector, and Bionic system property reads for the claimed boot state
evidenceUnits.availability: Comparable only when Widevine is supported, the plugin advertises L1, and the boot properties claim a locked verified state; devices advertising only L3 or honestly reporting an unlocked bootloader are reported as not comparable
evidenceUnits.trustBoundary: Crosses from values a userspace module can rewrite to key material held by the DRM trustlet, which a module can neither forge nor re-provision, so the comparison survives property spoofing and a forged attestation keybox
evidenceUnits.inferenceLimit: Proves the two statements are inconsistent, not which one is false or which tool caused it: an erased DRM credential can also follow a mainboard replacement or a device that never carried L1 provisioning, and no locked unmodified device has been measured, so the rate at which legitimate devices present this way is unknown

detections.name: ELF Text Integrity
detections.description: Compares selected libc, ART, and input-library non-writable executable PT_LOAD bytes with their file-backed ELF without changing page protections.

evidenceUnits.title: Mapped ELF text mismatch
evidenceUnits.observedObject: Selected non-writable executable PT_LOAD bytes and their backing ELF bytes
evidenceUnits.proposition: A compared executable segment differs from the corresponding file-backed ELF range
evidenceUnits.observationChannel: Public linker enumeration, process maps, memory reads, and backing-file reads
evidenceUnits.availability: Depends on module presence, resolved backing files, readable mappings, and supported ELF layout
evidenceUnits.trustBoundary: Both in-memory and file-backed observations are made from the potentially mediated process
evidenceUnits.inferenceLimit: A mismatch indicates code divergence but does not identify the modifier or prove malicious behavior

detections.name: Emulator Hardware Indicators
detections.description: Detects virtualized and emulated hardware environments using offscreen OpenGL ES renderers, ARM64 hardware timer registers, and scheduler jitter analysis.

evidenceUnits.title: Offscreen OpenGL ES renderer
evidenceUnits.observedObject: EGL display and OpenGL ES GL_RENDERER and GL_VENDOR strings
evidenceUnits.proposition: The offscreen OpenGL ES renderer identifies a software rasterizer or virtual machine graphics driver
evidenceUnits.observationChannel: EGL 1.4 and OpenGL ES 2.0 API
evidenceUnits.availability: Requires EGL display initialization and pbuffer surface support
evidenceUnits.trustBoundary: Vendor strings can be spoofed in modified emulator builds
evidenceUnits.inferenceLimit: Identifies known emulator rendering drivers; does not classify physical GPU variants

evidenceUnits.title: ARM64 hardware timer register deviation
evidenceUnits.observedObject: ARM64 cntvct_el0 and cntfrq_el0 virtual counter registers
evidenceUnits.proposition: The ARM64 virtual counter frequency or drift deviates significantly from CLOCK_MONOTONIC
evidenceUnits.observationChannel: ARM64 inline assembly instructions and POSIX monotonic clock
evidenceUnits.availability: Supported exclusively on 64-bit ARM (aarch64) platforms
evidenceUnits.trustBoundary: Hypervisors may trap or emulate timer register reads with overhead
evidenceUnits.inferenceLimit: Indicates virtualized counter timing characteristics; does not pinpoint hypervisor vendor

evidenceUnits.title: Scheduler yield jitter distribution
evidenceUnits.observedObject: POSIX sched_yield latency distribution across 32 iterations
evidenceUnits.proposition: The thread yield latency exhibits abnormally low coefficient of variation characteristic of deterministic virtualization
evidenceUnits.observationChannel: POSIX sched_yield and clock_gettime syscalls
evidenceUnits.availability: Requires monotonic clock access and thread scheduling privileges
evidenceUnits.trustBoundary: Physical system quiescence may occasionally reduce scheduling jitter
evidenceUnits.inferenceLimit: Statistical heuristic indicating virtualization; requires correlation with hardware signals

detections.name: Emulator System Profile
detections.description: Detects emulator environments through QEMU system properties, virtual hardware identifiers, build fingerprints, and emulator boot characteristics.

evidenceUnits.title: QEMU and virtual hardware system properties
evidenceUnits.observedObject: Bionic system properties associated with QEMU and Android emulator platforms
evidenceUnits.proposition: System properties explicitly declare QEMU or virtual hardware drivers
evidenceUnits.observationChannel: Bionic system-property API via direct syscall or __system_property_get
evidenceUnits.availability: Requires readable system property areas in /dev/__properties__
evidenceUnits.trustBoundary: Root processes may modify or unset properties using tools like resetprop
evidenceUnits.inferenceLimit: Identifies standard emulator platform property configurations

evidenceUnits.title: Emulator build fingerprint and model characteristics
evidenceUnits.observedObject: ro.build.fingerprint and device model properties
evidenceUnits.proposition: The system build fingerprint or product model matches generic emulator patterns
evidenceUnits.observationChannel: Bionic system-property API
evidenceUnits.availability: Requires access to Android build properties
evidenceUnits.trustBoundary: Fingerprints can be spoofed by custom ROMs or Magisk modules
evidenceUnits.inferenceLimit: Indicates build configuration origin; does not detect hardened hypervisor instances

detections.name: Kernel Integrity Check
detections.description: Checks kernel compilation signatures in /proc/version and uname, bootloader lock state from /proc/cmdline, and kptr_restrict address visibility in /proc/kallsyms, and cross-checks the kernel release the process inherited from Zygote against the live uname() release and its procfs exports.

evidenceUnits.title: Kernel and boot integrity posture
evidenceUnits.observedObject: Kernel build strings, version signatures, bootloader parameters, and kallsyms address visibility
evidenceUnits.proposition: An available kernel or boot observation matches a maintained integrity-posture rule
evidenceUnits.observationChannel: uname, /proc/version, /proc/cmdline, and /proc/kallsyms
evidenceUnits.availability: Each observation depends on kernel configuration, procfs permissions, and platform exposure
evidenceUnits.trustBoundary: The running kernel owns all returned sources and can conceal or rewrite them
evidenceUnits.inferenceLimit: A marker or visibility state is bounded evidence and does not prove a malicious custom kernel

evidenceUnits.title: Kernel release identity across sources
evidenceUnits.observedObject: The kernel release string as recorded in the os.version system property inherited from Zygote, returned by a live uname() call, and exported by /proc/sys/kernel/osrelease and /proc/version
evidenceUnits.proposition: Two readable sources report different kernel releases, which an unmodified device cannot do because the release cannot change while the kernel runs
evidenceUnits.observationChannel: System.getProperty("os.version") through JNI, the uname() syscall, and bounded procfs reads
evidenceUnits.availability: Comparable when at least two sources are readable; the Zygote snapshot and uname() normally are, while an app's SELinux domain usually cannot read the procfs exports
evidenceUnits.trustBoundary: Crosses from the release Zygote recorded before this app started to what the kernel returns now; a kernel hook can rewrite each live source, and an in-process hook can rewrite the Java property
evidenceUnits.inferenceLimit: A disagreement shows that some source was rewritten, not which one or by which tool; agreement is a concealable negative, because a spoof applied before Zygote initialises makes every source carry the same spoofed release

detections.name: Keystore Grant Chain Consistency
detections.description: Reads one Keystore key's attestation certificate chain twice, once by alias and once through a grant the application issues to its own uid, and compares them; a grant read-back that denies the key exists is graded separately, after a non-attested control key shows the grant path works. A stored chain is identical to every reader, so a difference proves the chain is being produced per lookup rather than returned from storage.

evidenceUnits.title: Alias-path and grant-path certificate chains
evidenceUnits.observedObject: The certificate chain of a freshly generated attested EC key, read through KeyStore.getCertificateChain and through KeyStoreManager.getGrantedCertificateChainFromId for the same key
evidenceUnits.proposition: The two readings of one key's certificate chain disagree in length or in a certificate digest, or the grant path denies that the key exists while a non-attested control key reads back through its grant, none of which storage can produce
evidenceUnits.observationChannel: AndroidKeyStore provider and the public android.security.keystore.KeyStoreManager grant API through a JNI collector
evidenceUnits.availability: Requires API 36 or later, where KeyStoreManager first ships; below that the check reports unavailable rather than clean, and attestation key generation must succeed
evidenceUnits.trustBoundary: Self-referential and carries no reference data, so it holds against an attestation chain that verifies to a genuine root: an interception layer must answer both lookup paths identically to stay consistent
evidenceUnits.inferenceLimit: Proves the chain is synthesised per lookup, not which layer synthesises it or whether the attestation content is false; a layer that answers both paths identically is invisible to this check, and an isolated-process reader, which would be a stronger second path, cannot reach the Keystore service on any device

detections.name: LSPosed/Xposed Maps Scan
detections.description: Scans /proc/self/maps for LSPosed, Xposed, EdXposed, and Riru framework libraries loaded into the process memory.

evidenceUnits.title: LSPosed or Xposed process-map marker
evidenceUnits.observedObject: Mapped paths and names in the current process
evidenceUnits.proposition: A process mapping matches a maintained LSPosed, Xposed, EdXposed, or Riru marker
evidenceUnits.observationChannel: /proc/self/maps parsing
evidenceUnits.availability: Depends on maps readability and marker visibility in the target process
evidenceUnits.trustBoundary: The process map view and parser can be filtered or hooked
evidenceUnits.inferenceLimit: A marker supports framework presence in this process but not module scope or system-wide activation

detections.name: LSPosed SELinux Policy Oracle
detections.description: Uses a controlled app-zygote SELinux policy snapshot to observe LSPosed and Xposed-specific allow rules.

evidenceUnits.title: LSPosed-related SELinux policy oracle
evidenceUnits.observedObject: Controlled app-zygote SELinux allow-rule decisions and validation controls
evidenceUnits.proposition: A validated policy query permits a maintained LSPosed or Xposed-specific rule
evidenceUnits.observationChannel: Native and hidden-framework SELinux policy queries in an app-zygote carrier
evidenceUnits.availability: Requires carrier setup, stable controls, valid contexts, and available query sources
evidenceUnits.trustBoundary: The oracle reports source agreement and trust rather than assuming every query path is independent
evidenceUnits.inferenceLimit: An allowed rule is policy evidence and does not prove that LSPosed is injected into this process

detections.name: Memory FD Anomaly
detections.description: Correlates executable memfd, ashmem, deleted mappings, and file descriptors while retaining generic anonymous-memory artifacts as telemetry.

evidenceUnits.title: Executable memory and FD artifact
evidenceUnits.observedObject: Executable memfd, ashmem, deleted mappings, and correlated file-descriptor targets
evidenceUnits.proposition: An executable memory or FD artifact satisfies either a detector signal rule or a non-attributing research candidate rule
evidenceUnits.observationChannel: /proc/self/maps and /proc/self/fd correlation
evidenceUnits.availability: Depends on maps and fd-directory readability and parseable targets
evidenceUnits.trustBoundary: Both procfs sources are app-local and can be filtered by concealment
evidenceUnits.inferenceLimit: Direct markers may support assessment; generic executable or deleted artifacts remain research data and do not establish instrumentation or privilege

detections.name: Memory Linker Visibility
detections.description: Cross-checks public dl_iterate_phdr load ranges with /proc/self/maps and verifies standard library symbol resolution boundaries (GOT/PLT integrity) without private linker symbols.

evidenceUnits.title: Linker and process-map view consistency
evidenceUnits.observedObject: Normalized module visibility relationships between dl_iterate_phdr objects, executable process mappings, and resolved symbol addresses
evidenceUnits.proposition: The linker and process-map views agree or expose a directional module-visibility mismatch or symbol resolution escape
evidenceUnits.observationChannel: dl_iterate_phdr, dlsym, and /proc/self/maps range comparison
evidenceUnits.availability: Requires public linker enumeration, dlsym symbol resolution, and readable process maps
evidenceUnits.trustBoundary: The user-visible linker tables and process maps can both be mediated and are not independent kernel attestation
evidenceUnits.inferenceLimit: Linker-only mismatches, maps-only hidden modules, or symbol resolution escapes outside valid load ranges indicate memory tampering or hooking

detections.name: Memory Maps Anomaly
detections.description: Reports non-ART writable, anonymous, or deleted executable mappings, smaps dirty-page code modifications, and suspicious signal handler registrations.

evidenceUnits.title: Executable mapping anomaly
evidenceUnits.observedObject: Non-ART writable, anonymous, deleted executable mappings, smaps dirty code pages, and signal handler targets
evidenceUnits.proposition: A normalized process-map entry, smaps dirty page, or signal handler target satisfies an anomaly rule
evidenceUnits.observationChannel: /proc/self/maps parsing, /proc/self/smaps dirty page audit, and sigaction query
evidenceUnits.availability: Depends on maps/smaps readability and sigaction accessibility
evidenceUnits.trustBoundary: The process map and smaps views can be filtered or rewritten
evidenceUnits.inferenceLimit: Generic mapping anomalies have legitimate producers. Anonymous or instrumentation-owned signal handlers and writable executable mappings drive the assessment; dirty system code pages are collected as context only, because relocation and copy-on-write dirty executable pages on ordinary devices and the size thresholds are not yet calibrated against a clean baseline.

detections.name: Mount Table Integrity
detections.description: Detects framework-specific mount markers and cross-checks mountinfo against statx and statfs kernel observations; mount ID sequence gaps are recorded as telemetry.

evidenceUnits.title: Mount-table marker
evidenceUnits.observedObject: Mount-table rows and normalized mount relationships
evidenceUnits.proposition: An app-visible mount row satisfies a framework-specific or bounded generic mount rule
evidenceUnits.observationChannel: /proc/self/mountinfo parsing
evidenceUnits.availability: Requires at least one required mount source to be readable and parseable
evidenceUnits.trustBoundary: The process mount namespace can differ from init and can be filtered by concealment
evidenceUnits.inferenceLimit: Generic rules are not framework attribution, and absence is limited to the visible namespace

evidenceUnits.title: Kernel and mount-table view consistency
evidenceUnits.observedObject: Mount IDs and filesystem types returned for selected paths
evidenceUnits.proposition: statx or statfs observations agree or disagree with the parsed mount-table view
evidenceUnits.observationChannel: statx mount ID, statfs type, and mount-table comparison
evidenceUnits.availability: Depends on syscall support, selected path visibility, and readable mount sources
evidenceUnits.trustBoundary: Syscalls and procfs are separate app-visible channels but can share kernel mediation
evidenceUnits.inferenceLimit: Agreement does not prove global mount integrity; unavailable sources must remain explicit

evidenceUnits.title: Mount namespace observation
evidenceUnits.observedObject: Mount ID sequences, mount namespace identifiers, and root mount propagation
evidenceUnits.proposition: The app-visible mount environment has the recorded structural properties, or the process shares the init mount namespace
evidenceUnits.observationChannel: Parsed /proc/self/mountinfo plus the /proc/self/ns/mnt and /proc/1/ns/mnt namespace links
evidenceUnits.availability: Varies by the individual source and is retained even when no finding is produced
evidenceUnits.trustBoundary: Telemetry describes the observed process view rather than a privileged global view
evidenceUnits.inferenceLimit: Telemetry fields do not prove global mount configuration. Mount ID sequence gaps occur on unmodified phones and are not evidence of mount hiding; only a shared init namespace contributes a signal.

detections.name: Devpts Permission Anomaly
detections.description: Checks /dev/pts/ pseudo-terminal permissions and SELinux contexts. KernelSU hooks may stamp PTYs with root ownership or ksu_file context.

evidenceUnits.title: Devpts ownership and context anomaly
evidenceUnits.observedObject: Visible pseudo-terminal ownership, permissions, freshness, and SELinux context
evidenceUnits.proposition: A tested pseudo-terminal satisfies an explicit root-related metadata or context rule
evidenceUnits.observationChannel: devpts enumeration, stat metadata, and SELinux file context
evidenceUnits.availability: Depends on devpts visibility, an available PTY, and readable metadata or contexts
evidenceUnits.trustBoundary: The process-visible devpts mount and context view may be mediated
evidenceUnits.inferenceLimit: PTY metadata can have non-root producers and does not prove application privilege

detections.name: Native Root Paths
detections.description: Probes filesystem paths associated with KernelSU, APatch, and Magisk using multi-confirmation (stat/lstat/open) to detect root management artifacts.

evidenceUnits.title: Native root-framework path artifact
evidenceUnits.observedObject: Filesystem paths associated with KernelSU, APatch, or Magisk
evidenceUnits.proposition: A maintained framework path was confirmed by the recorded native path operations
evidenceUnits.observationChannel: Native stat, lstat, and open confirmations
evidenceUnits.availability: Depends on path visibility, permissions, and process mount namespace
evidenceUnits.trustBoundary: The app-local VFS can be filtered by concealment or kernel changes
evidenceUnits.inferenceLimit: A path artifact does not prove that the associated provider is active for this process

detections.name: Native Root Interface Probe
detections.description: Detects KernelSU, APatch, and native root frameworks by probing kernel prctl, supercall latency, cgroups, and driver file descriptors.

evidenceUnits.title: KernelSU and native root protocol response
evidenceUnits.observedObject: Kernel responses to root prctl commands, supercall latency, cgroup allocations, and driver file descriptors
evidenceUnits.proposition: The kernel interface or process environment returned a response satisfying a native root framework indicator
evidenceUnits.observationChannel: Direct native prctl, syscall latency benchmarking, /proc/self/cgroup, and /proc/self/fd
evidenceUnits.availability: Requires kernel interfaces and procfs nodes to execute without interception that suppresses or emulates responses
evidenceUnits.trustBoundary: The kernel syscall boundary is below ordinary Java mediation but can be modified by the kernel
evidenceUnits.inferenceLimit: The response identifies protocol compatibility or anomaly, not the full privilege granted to the app. The supercall latency deviation is a timing measurement taken without CPU pinning or frequency control, so it is treated as moderate corroboration rather than a direct marker.

detections.name: Native Root SELinux Policy Oracle
detections.description: Uses a controlled app-zygote SELinux policy snapshot to observe Magisk, KernelSU, ADB-root, and su-specific allow rules.

evidenceUnits.title: Root-related SELinux policy oracle
evidenceUnits.observedObject: Controlled app-zygote SELinux allow-rule decisions and validation controls
evidenceUnits.proposition: A validated policy query permits a maintained Magisk, KernelSU, ADB-root, or su-related rule
evidenceUnits.observationChannel: Native and hidden-framework SELinux policy queries in an app-zygote carrier
evidenceUnits.availability: Requires carrier setup, stable positive and negative controls, and at least one trusted query source
evidenceUnits.trustBoundary: Java-controlled query sources are weaker than native sources and their trust tier remains explicit
evidenceUnits.inferenceLimit: An allowed rule is policy evidence and does not prove current process injection or granted root

detections.name: SUSFS Side-Channel Probe
detections.description: Detects SUSFS (KernelSU filesystem hiding module) via a side-channel: a child process attempts setresuid and SUSFS kills it with SIGKILL instead of returning EPERM.

evidenceUnits.title: SUSFS syscall side-channel
evidenceUnits.observedObject: Child-process termination behavior during a controlled setresuid probe
evidenceUnits.proposition: The child was terminated with the detector-defined signal pattern instead of returning the expected permission error
evidenceUnits.observationChannel: Forked child, setresuid syscall, and parent wait status
evidenceUnits.availability: Requires process creation, syscall execution, and reliable wait-status collection
evidenceUnits.trustBoundary: The kernel controls syscall and signal behavior and can intentionally imitate or hide the pattern
evidenceUnits.inferenceLimit: The side-channel is associated with tested SUSFS behavior but is not a universal or version-independent proof

detections.name: Package Storage Visibility
detections.description: Probes Android data and OBB package paths for canonical and Unicode alias visibility.

evidenceUnits.title: Package storage path visibility
evidenceUnits.observedObject: Canonical or Unicode-aliased package data and OBB paths
evidenceUnits.proposition: A storage path associated with an indicator package is visible through at least one tested representation
evidenceUnits.observationChannel: stat, access, open, and directory-list probes over canonical and transformed paths
evidenceUnits.availability: Depends on external-storage layout, target presence, package isolation, FUSE or BPF behavior, and permissions
evidenceUnits.trustBoundary: The app observes a platform- and namespace-mediated storage view
evidenceUnits.inferenceLimit: Path visibility does not prove package execution, root activation, or a universal Unicode bypass

evidenceUnits.title: Path representation differential
evidenceUnits.observedObject: Different results returned for canonical and transformed package-storage paths
evidenceUnits.proposition: The tested path representations produced a platform-level visibility differential
evidenceUnits.observationChannel: Paired canonical and Unicode path probes
evidenceUnits.availability: Requires a comparable probe pair and sufficient platform response data
evidenceUnits.trustBoundary: The differential reflects the app-visible storage stack rather than an unmediated filesystem ground truth
evidenceUnits.inferenceLimit: The differential is telemetry and is not attributed to a root or concealment framework

detections.name: Prologue Scanner
detections.description: Compares resolved libc and dynamic-linker function entries with their backing ELF bytes to identify runtime code redirection or modification.

evidenceUnits.title: Resolved function-entry integrity
evidenceUnits.observedObject: Resolved libc or linker function entry bytes and their backing ELF bytes
evidenceUnits.proposition: A resolved function entry is redirected outside its expected module or differs from backing bytes
evidenceUnits.observationChannel: dlsym, dladdr, in-memory bytes, and backing ELF comparison
evidenceUnits.availability: Depends on symbol resolution, expected module availability, and readable backing ELF data
evidenceUnits.trustBoundary: Dynamic linker APIs and process memory are observable within the potentially instrumented process
evidenceUnits.inferenceLimit: Modification supports code-redirection evidence but does not attribute a framework or intent

evidenceUnits.title: Function-entry pattern
evidenceUnits.observedObject: Architecture-specific branch and trampoline-like entry-byte patterns
evidenceUnits.proposition: The resolved entry bytes match the recorded descriptive pattern
evidenceUnits.observationChannel: Bounded architecture-specific byte classification
evidenceUnits.availability: Requires a supported architecture and readable function-entry bytes
evidenceUnits.trustBoundary: The pattern is derived from the same process-visible bytes as the integrity comparison
evidenceUnits.inferenceLimit: Pattern telemetry is diagnostic-only and does not independently affect assessment

detections.name: Property Area Physical Residue
detections.description: Inspects Bionic property area memory structures for prop_info serial anomalies, value-length mismatches, and dirty trailing bytes left by in-place property tampering tools such as resetprop.

evidenceUnits.title: Property serial and length consistency
evidenceUnits.observedObject: Bionic prop_info serial word encoding value length and update counter
evidenceUnits.proposition: A system property exhibits an update counter on an immutable read-only property or a mismatch between the serial length field and the string value
evidenceUnits.observationChannel: Direct parsing of process-mapped /dev/__properties__/* areas via /proc/self/maps
evidenceUnits.availability: Available when Bionic property areas are mapped into process memory and format matches PROP_AREA_MAGIC
evidenceUnits.trustBoundary: Reads property-area memory directly in our address space, bypassing libc property accessors that may be hooked
evidenceUnits.inferenceLimit: Dynamic non-ro properties legitimately increment serial counters; only ro.* properties and strict length mismatches are considered anomalies

evidenceUnits.title: Property value trailing buffer residue
evidenceUnits.observedObject: Unused bytes in prop_info value buffer past the initial NUL terminator
evidenceUnits.proposition: A property value buffer contains non-zero bytes after its terminating NUL byte, indicating an in-place string overwrite without buffer zeroing
evidenceUnits.observationChannel: Direct byte inspection of mapped prop_info structures in memory
evidenceUnits.availability: Requires read access to process memory maps containing property area files
evidenceUnits.trustBoundary: Operates directly on mapped physical buffer bytes in process address space
evidenceUnits.inferenceLimit: Non-zero trailing bytes occur when an existing property is replaced with a shorter string (e.g. userdebug replaced with user); an overwrite with equal or longer string does not leave trailing bytes

detections.name: Runtime Instrumentation
detections.description: Correlates portable process maps, FD, thread, and public linker markers while keeping generic runtime artifacts as telemetry.

evidenceUnits.title: Direct runtime instrumentation marker
evidenceUnits.observedObject: Process mappings, file descriptors, threads, or linker objects containing maintained direct markers
evidenceUnits.proposition: A portable process observation matches a maintained runtime instrumentation marker
evidenceUnits.observationChannel: procfs maps, fd and task directories, plus public linker enumeration
evidenceUnits.availability: Depends on procfs readability and linker enumeration within the target process
evidenceUnits.trustBoundary: All channels are app-local and can be altered by in-process or kernel mediation
evidenceUnits.inferenceLimit: Marker attribution is bounded to the matched string and does not establish device-level compromise

evidenceUnits.title: Generic runtime anomaly telemetry
evidenceUnits.observedObject: Portable process artifacts that are non-unique to instrumentation frameworks
evidenceUnits.proposition: A generic runtime artifact matching a telemetry rule is present
evidenceUnits.observationChannel: procfs and public linker observations
evidenceUnits.availability: Depends on the underlying process sources being readable
evidenceUnits.trustBoundary: The observations are app-local and may be mediated
evidenceUnits.inferenceLimit: Generic anomalies are telemetry-only and must not be promoted to findings without a new validated rule

detections.name: Read-Write Paths Checking
detections.description: Checks for the presence of critical system paths that are writable, which can indicate a compromised environment.

evidenceUnits.title: Critical system path writability
evidenceUnits.observedObject: Selected critical system filesystem paths
evidenceUnits.proposition: The app-local permission probe reports a critical path as writable
evidenceUnits.observationChannel: Filesystem access permission checks
evidenceUnits.availability: Depends on path visibility and the semantics of the tested access operation
evidenceUnits.trustBoundary: The result is scoped to the app mount namespace, credentials, and mediated VFS view
evidenceUnits.inferenceLimit: Writability can have legitimate causes and does not identify a modification mechanism

detections.name: SELinux Global Enforcement
detections.description: Cross-checks global SELinux enforcement observations, infers enforcement from a refused read of the DAC-readable enforce node, and probes enforce-node permissions without writing.

evidenceUnits.title: SELinux enforcement state
evidenceUnits.observedObject: Enforcement state reported by available SELinux sources, or inferred from an EACCES refusal to read the enforce node
evidenceUnits.proposition: One or more available sources report the current SELinux enforcement mode
evidenceUnits.observationChannel: selinuxfs and libselinux read-only queries, plus stat() of the enforce node when its read is refused with EACCES
evidenceUnits.availability: Depends on selinuxfs visibility and library availability; the read-denial inference needs selinuxfs confirmed by statfs and a DAC mode that permits the read, measured by stat() or taken from the kernel constant 0644 when stat() is refused
evidenceUnits.trustBoundary: Each source is independently mediated and source disagreement remains explicit
evidenceUnits.inferenceLimit: A reported enforcing state does not establish policy integrity; an inferred enforcing state shows only that the app's own domain is enforced, says nothing about other domains, and is defeated by a hook that makes open() return EACCES; unavailable sources are not negative evidence

evidenceUnits.title: SELinux enforce-node access
evidenceUnits.observedObject: The app process permission result for the SELinux enforce node
evidenceUnits.proposition: The enforce node returned the recorded writable or denied result without performing a write, and its DAC mode is recorded when a read is refused
evidenceUnits.observationChannel: Write-mode open without writing, and stat(), against /sys/fs/selinux/enforce
evidenceUnits.availability: Requires the enforce node to be visible enough to attempt the permission check
evidenceUnits.trustBoundary: The VFS and SELinux permission path can be mediated
evidenceUnits.inferenceLimit: A permission result is contextual and does not alone prove policy tampering

evidenceUnits.title: SELinux cross-source consistency
evidenceUnits.observedObject: A contradictory combination of enforcement and filesystem permission observations
evidenceUnits.proposition: Available SELinux observations satisfy a detector-defined contradiction rule; a disagreement that depends on an inferred answer is graded below one between two read sources
evidenceUnits.observationChannel: Cross-check of enforcement sources, selinuxfs state, and permission probes
evidenceUnits.availability: Requires the specific sources needed by a contradiction rule
evidenceUnits.trustBoundary: The rule compares mediated sources and does not create an external ground truth
evidenceUnits.inferenceLimit: The contradiction supports an anomaly claim but not attribution to a particular root framework

detections.name: SU Binary Checking
detections.description: Classifies visible su-related paths by object type, resolved metadata, executable mode, and bounded ELF-magic evidence.

evidenceUnits.title: Visible su-related artifact
evidenceUnits.observedObject: A resolved filesystem object at an su candidate path
evidenceUnits.proposition: An su-related artifact with recorded object and executable-format properties is visible
evidenceUnits.observationChannel: Fixed-path access, lstat, O_PATH open, fstat, mode, and bounded ELF-magic inspection
evidenceUnits.availability: Available only for candidate paths visible and inspectable from the application sandbox
evidenceUnits.trustBoundary: App-local VFS view and user-space parsing can be filtered or hooked
evidenceUnits.inferenceLimit: Visibility does not prove successful privilege escalation or identify the current root provider

detections.name: SU Context Checking
detections.description: Checks /proc/self/attr/current and per-process SELinux contexts for root-related anomalies.

evidenceUnits.title: Process SELinux context anomaly
evidenceUnits.observedObject: SELinux contexts exposed for the current and visible processes
evidenceUnits.proposition: A visible process context matches a root-related or otherwise abnormal context rule
evidenceUnits.observationChannel: /proc process attribute files
evidenceUnits.availability: Depends on procfs visibility and permission to read process attributes
evidenceUnits.trustBoundary: The process-visible procfs and SELinux views may be mediated
evidenceUnits.inferenceLimit: A context match is an indicator and does not prove that this application can obtain root

detections.name: System Property Source Integrity
detections.description: Cross-checks equivalent Android property sources and parses property areas with explicit failure states.

evidenceUnits.title: Equivalent property-source consistency
evidenceUnits.observedObject: Equivalent Android property values read through multiple sources
evidenceUnits.proposition: Available sources either agree or satisfy an explicit mismatch rule for the same property
evidenceUnits.observationChannel: Comparison across the bionic callback accessor, the bionic legacy accessor, android.os.SystemProperties, a forked getprop, the parsed property-area bytes, android.os.Build, and /proc/cmdline boot parameters
evidenceUnits.availability: A comparison is possible only when enough equivalent sources return usable values
evidenceUnits.trustBoundary: All user-space sources can share mediation; agreement is not proof of kernel-level integrity. Only /proc/cmdline sits below user space, and only the property-area source bypasses the bionic accessor
evidenceUnits.inferenceLimit: Strength is graded by which source is the outlier rather than by how many sources disagree: a kernel-versus-userspace or property-area-versus-accessor contradiction is STRONG, a Java-API or separate-process outlier is MODERATE, and an android.os.Build outlier is WEAK because the property may simply have changed after process start. Values are trimmed, lowercased and boolean-aliased before comparison, so a case-only or formatting-only spoof is not detected. Missing or failed sources remain collection state rather than negative evidence

evidenceUnits.title: Property-area allocation integrity
evidenceUnits.observedObject: Parsed property-area allocation and unreferenced byte ranges
evidenceUnits.proposition: Visible property areas exhibit structural Trie integrity without orphaned unreferenced allocations
evidenceUnits.observationChannel: Direct read-only parsing of visible property-area files
evidenceUnits.availability: Depends on path visibility, permissions, and compatible property-area format
evidenceUnits.trustBoundary: The app-visible files and parser remain below the kernel or privileged service trust boundary
evidenceUnits.inferenceLimit: Unreferenced allocation indicates modified or deleted Trie nodes (e.g. via resetprop), though atypical OEM layouts remain possible

detections.name: TEE Attestation Validation
detections.description: Validates a fresh Android Keystore attestation challenge, certificate chain, trust anchor, revocation status, and RootOfTrust consistency.

evidenceUnits.title: Keystore attestation chain and RootOfTrust
evidenceUnits.observedObject: A fresh Android Keystore attestation response, certificate chain, revocation snapshot, challenge, and RootOfTrust fields
evidenceUnits.proposition: The returned attestation artifacts satisfy or violate the recorded cryptographic and structural validation rules
evidenceUnits.observationChannel: Android Keystore key generation and offline certificate or extension validation
evidenceUnits.availability: Depends on Keystore support, certificate availability, parseable extensions, and bundled trust data
evidenceUnits.trustBoundary: Hardware-backed claims originate below the app, while local validation and revocation freshness remain app-managed
evidenceUnits.inferenceLimit: Local attestation is not equivalent to server-side nonce policy or Play Integrity and may be unavailable on supported devices

detections.name: TEE Keystore Consistency
detections.description: Checks public Android Keystore signature, lifecycle, and certificate-entry invariants while retaining AES and StrongBox observations as diagnostics.

evidenceUnits.title: Android Keystore public-API consistency
evidenceUnits.observedObject: Required signature, key lifecycle, and certificate-entry invariants plus optional capability diagnostics
evidenceUnits.proposition: A required public Keystore invariant completed consistently or returned a recorded contradiction
evidenceUnits.observationChannel: Android Keystore public APIs
evidenceUnits.availability: Depends on algorithm, provider, and optional StrongBox capabilities
evidenceUnits.trustBoundary: The app observes framework API behavior and does not directly inspect TEE implementation state
evidenceUnits.inferenceLimit: Optional AES and StrongBox observations are diagnostic; a contradiction is not root-provider attribution

detections.name: TEE Oversized Challenge
detections.description: Checks whether Android Keystore enforces the documented attestation challenge-size limit without attributing the result to a specific root tool.

evidenceUnits.title: Attestation challenge-size enforcement
evidenceUnits.observedObject: Keystore behavior for a challenge exceeding the documented size limit
evidenceUnits.proposition: The tested Keystore path accepted or rejected the oversized challenge at the recorded stage
evidenceUnits.observationChannel: Android Keystore attestation key-generation request
evidenceUnits.availability: Depends on Keystore availability and successful setup and cleanup of the test alias
evidenceUnits.trustBoundary: The result reflects the public Keystore stack exposed to the application
evidenceUnits.inferenceLimit: Unexpected behavior is a bounded consistency anomaly and is not attributed to a particular root tool

detections.name: VDSO Integrity
detections.description: Cross-checks the VDSO mapping, AT_SYSINFO_EHDR, ELF load ranges, public linker ownership, and available kernel-helper symbol ownership.

evidenceUnits.title: VDSO mapping and ownership consistency
evidenceUnits.observedObject: The VDSO mapping, AT_SYSINFO_EHDR, ELF load ranges, linker owner, and available helper symbol
evidenceUnits.proposition: Available VDSO observations satisfy or violate explicit mapping and ownership consistency rules
evidenceUnits.observationChannel: procfs maps, auxv, ELF parsing, public linker enumeration, and symbol resolution
evidenceUnits.availability: Individual checks depend on readable maps and auxv plus available linker and symbol data
evidenceUnits.trustBoundary: The app-local channels may be mediated and are not independent kernel attestation
evidenceUnits.inferenceLimit: A consistency violation is an anomaly and does not identify the modification mechanism

detections.name: Cross-Process Descriptor Forensics
detections.description: Cross-checks three independent kernel views of the process descriptor table in the host process and in a helper process forked fresh from Zygote, and carries a cross-process trap descriptor as telemetry.

evidenceUnits.title: Descriptor table view differential
evidenceUnits.observedObject: The open file descriptors of the host process and of a dedicated helper process, as reported by three independent kernel interfaces
evidenceUnits.proposition: The descriptor table, the /proc/self/fd lookup path and the /proc/self/fd iteration path disagree about the same descriptor across repeated sweeps
evidenceUnits.observationChannel: fcntl(F_GETFD) against readlink(/proc/self/fd/<n>) against readdir(/proc/self/fd), repeated in the host process and in an android:process helper
evidenceUnits.availability: Requires a readable /proc/self/fd; the comparison is skipped when procfs resolves no descriptors at all
evidenceUnits.trustBoundary: A kernel-resident hook that filters both the lookup and the iteration path consistently would defeat the comparison, as would one that also intercepts fcntl
evidenceUnits.inferenceLimit: A stable disagreement is a contradiction in the kernel's own descriptor accounting and needs no device threshold, but it identifies procfs filtering in general rather than any specific tool. Reported at MODERATE while the detector is EXPERIMENTAL because no clean-device baseline exists for the residual race rate.

evidenceUnits.title: Cross-process trap descriptor
evidenceUnits.observedObject: An unlinked, app-private trap descriptor transferred to the helper process over Binder
evidenceUnits.proposition: The trap descriptor did not survive transfer to a separately specialized process intact
evidenceUnits.observationChannel: ParcelFileDescriptor transfer, then fstat, pread of the signature payload and readlink of /proc/self/fd in the receiving process
evidenceUnits.availability: Requires the helper process to bind and the host cache directory to be writable
evidenceUnits.trustBoundary: The descriptor is app-private and unlinked, so only a process already holding it could alter it
evidenceUnits.inferenceLimit: Telemetry only; this channel can never move the detector outcome. The descriptor is installed into the helper process by the binder driver after that process has finished specializing, so Zygisk-style specialization-time descriptor sanitization cannot reach it and no result here supports a tamper claim.

detections.name: Dynamic Linker Namespace Audit
detections.description: Audits loaded shared libraries via dl_iterate_phdr, inspects thread comm names, and verifies file descriptor isolation traps.

evidenceUnits.title: Suspicious loaded-library path
evidenceUnits.observedObject: Shared objects enumerated by the process dynamic linker, task comm names, and anonymous trap file descriptors
evidenceUnits.proposition: A loaded object path matches an injection-related rule, or a task comm name / FD trap reveals an active runtime framework
evidenceUnits.observationChannel: dl_iterate_phdr public linker enumeration, /proc/self/task/*/comm, and anonymous FD verification
evidenceUnits.availability: Limited to objects and task directories exposed in the target process
evidenceUnits.trustBoundary: In-process hooks can alter linker enumeration, task comm strings, or file descriptors
evidenceUnits.inferenceLimit: A suspicious library path, thread name, or FD anomaly supports injection evidence but may not uniquely identify Zygisk

detections.name: Zygisk Dirty Pages Scan
detections.description: Scans /proc/self/smaps for executable system-library code split into one-page dirty regions, the footprint of in-place code patching, and records per-region dirt and heap allocation entropy as context.

evidenceUnits.title: Dirty executable system-library page
evidenceUnits.observedObject: Private or shared dirty counts for executable system-library mappings and mallinfo2 heap allocation ratios
evidenceUnits.proposition: An executable system-library mapping has been split into one-page regions carrying dirty pages
evidenceUnits.observationChannel: /proc/self/smaps parsing and mallinfo2 allocator queries
evidenceUnits.availability: Depends on smaps readability, recognized system-library paths, and mallinfo2 support (API >= 30)
evidenceUnits.trustBoundary: The process-visible procfs view and allocator state can be filtered by in-process or kernel concealment
evidenceUnits.inferenceLimit: One-page dirty regions show that code was patched in place, not who patched it: an inline-hooking SDK in the host app leaves the same shape as an injected framework, and neither implies root. Per-region dirt and heap fragmentation are context only and do not affect the assessment.
